title: Kamala, the stretchy heroine.
lines: This is Kamala.
Kamala is a girl from a city in America.
Her family comes from Pakistan.
Kamala loves drawing.
She draws superheroes.
Her big hero is Captain Marvel.
Kamala dreams of being a heroine herself.
But she thinks: I'm just Kamala.
Nothing special.
Kamala's grandma gives her an old bracelet.
It has pretty stones in it.
It belongs to our family, says Grandma.
Kamala puts the bracelet on.
And then something very strange happens.
The bracelet starts to glow.
Purple and blue.
Light comes out of her hands.
Now Kamala can make shiny pieces of light.
She can make stairs with them.
Or a big hand.
Or a shield.
And she can make her arm really long.
Longer and longer, as long as an elephant's trunk.
Kamala makes a suit.
Blue and red, with a yellow lightning bolt.
Her mum sews it for her.
Her best friend Bruno makes a mask.
One day there's a festival in the city.
There's music, there's tasty food and there are lots and lots of people.
Suddenly a strong wind blows.
A big advertising board starts to wobble.
It's going to fall.
Right onto the people!
Kamala doesn't hesitate.
She makes a giant hand of light.
She catches the board.
Pfff, it's heavy.
Bruno shouts: You can do it, Kamala!
She carefully puts the board down on the ground.
Nobody is hurt.
Then Kamala hears a child crying.
A little boy has lost his balloon.
The balloon is already floating high up.
Kamala stretches out her arm.
Longer and longer.
She grabs the string and gives the balloon back.
The people clap.
Who is that?
That's Ms Marvel!
Kamala goes home and eats with her family.
They eat rice and tasty curry.
Grandma winks.
She knows the secret.
Kamala smiles.
Now she knows that she is special.
Because she's just herself.
The end.
